history.recommendation_text: The Board recommends that the Administration review the potential outside activities of experts of sanctions committees to ensure that prior approval is sought and follow up on the 17 cases of potential conflict of interest and take appropriate action.
history.administration_response: The recommendation was implemented. The Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs completed its review of 17 cases of potential outside activities identified by the Board in September 2025. The Security Council Affairs Division of the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs consulted relevant experts, verified their explanations via open-source information and sought further clarification as needed. The review confirmed that two individuals were not experts on sanctions panels; the remaining 15 experts all properly disclosed external activities to the United Nations in advance, with no unreported outside work, unauthorized payments or conflicts of interest identified. In coordination with the Ethics Office, the Executive Office of the Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs and the Department of Peace Operations, and the Department of Operational Support, the Security Council Affairs Division assessed and strengthened its oversight and compliance frameworks. It enhanced pre-selection conflict-of-interest screening and ongoing monitoring of experts’ external activities. Beyond mandatory signed declarations under the Secretary- General’s bulletin on regulations governing the status, basic rights and duties of officials other than Secretariat officials, and experts on mission (ST/SGB/2002/9), experts are required to disclose outside activities for internal review and clearance and attend Ethics Office induction briefings, and are subject to mid-term open-source checks. The Department of Political and Peacebuilding Affairs will roll out improved training on external engagement obligations and conflict- of-interest rules. In December 2025, it also used the annual inter-panel workshop in New York to remind all sanctions experts of mandatory disclosure and prior approval requirements, with this obligation repeatedly reinforced during regular panel visits to New York.
history.board_assessment: In line with the Board’s recommendation, the Administration has reviewed the 17 cases of potential outside activities, further strengthened its monitoring of experts’ external activities and revised the draft guidance on the management of experts’ outside activities. We consider this recommendation to be implemented.
